action: Review exposure, access controls and monitoring for activity that alters business records or approval processes, as CERT-In advises; the advisory itself was not read, so check cert-in.org.in for its full recommendations.
date_note: The advisory is described only as 'recent' and is not dated in the article; the date is the IANS article's own date.
exec: CERT-In says attackers alter business records or approval processes to divert funds, beyond payment APIs, and that targets now include providers supporting government payment processes.
plain: India's cyber agency warns that criminals use AI tools to manipulate how businesses handle payments, so funds are diverted through business processes. It says banks are not the only targets.

sources.name: Telangana Today (IANS): CERT-In warns of AI-driven cyberattacks targeting business payment systems

summary: According to an IANS report, a recent CERT-In advisory says cybercriminals use AI-powered tools to manipulate business payment workflows and carry out unauthorised transactions. CERT-In says attacks now extend to technology service providers supporting government entities' payment processes and platforms handling vendor or partner payouts, not only banks. It says the concern is not limited to the security of payment APIs: attackers alter business records or approval processes to divert funds.
title: CERT-In warns AI-powered tools are used to manipulate business payment workflows, IANS reports

validation.note: One publisher (IANS via Telangana Today) read; Moneycontrol's article on the same advisory would not load; the CERT-In advisory itself was not read.

review.note: Against Telangana Today/IANS: removed unsupported 'transaction may pass usual application and approval checks' (article: attackers alter business records or approval processes to divert funds); 'government-linked payment processes' now 'government entities' payment processes'; plain and exec aligned
